title: Release Playbook Dry Run — Notes and Action Items
content:
Context:
This doc captures notes from the release playbook dry run we ran on 2025-11-03. The goal was to validate the emergency hotfix workflow end-to-end (detection -> patch -> rollback) across Dedicated and Hosted environments, exercise communications, and surface gaps in runbook steps and tooling integration. This is a working-note style doc; lots of TODOs and follow-ups below.

Attendees (onsite + remote):
- Aisha Patel (Release Eng, facilitator)
- Marco Li (Serving Runtime)
- Sofia Ramos (SRE / Oncall)
- Ethan Campbell (Platform Eng - CI/CD)
- Priya Narayanan (Product - Hosted API)
- Jordan Kim (Security)
- Observers: two new SRE hires (shadow)

Agenda:
1) Quick overview of playbook changes since v1 (Aisha)
2) Inject failure (simulated degradation on dedicated pool) and walk through detection/alerting
3) Patch branch -> canary -> full rollout -> rollback scenarios
4) Communications and customer-facing messaging template checks
5) Post-run retrospective and action items

High-level summary of run:
- Injected a CPU-saturation spike on a Dedicated GPU pool using the chaos harness (Marco/Ethan).
- Alerting fired (latency SLO breach) but pager escalation delay was ~3.5 minutes due to oncall coverage overlap; this is longer than our target of 2 minutes.
- We triaged and produced a minimal patch (runtime config flip to disable continuous batching for affected nodes). Patch build + CI took ~9 minutes (goal < 5).
- Canary rollout to 5% of traffic succeeded in restoring SLOs on canary nodes; however, the automatic fallback policy in routing did not trigger because the canary label was not propagated to traffic router metadata (bug traced to PR in infra).
- Manual traffic shift performed by Sofia through the console; full rollout completed after additional validation.
- We exercised rollback path: simulated bad model variant push; rollback worked but left KV-cache warmup issues (higher latency for several minutes post-rollback).

Detailed notes (chronological):
- 09:00 — Kickoff: walked through updated playbook (noted new step for verifying canary labels in routing metadata).
- 09:10 — Failure injected: CPU saturation -> increased request queueing -> latency spike. Alert rule "latency_slo_breach_v2" evaluated and paged.
- 09:14 — Pager received by oncall (Sofia); playbook step 1 (identify impacted route/model) completed. We discovered ambiguity in step 1: which dashboard is primary? SREs used Observability > Per-route view; product wanted ModelOps dashboard. Need to consolidate.
- 09:18 — Quick attempt to auto-run rollback via the orchestration play (release-orchestrator) failed: auth token expired for the dry-run service account. Token refresh is manual in prod; for dry-run we need a service-account fixture that auto-refreshes.
- 09:21 — Patch branch created (hotfix/disable-batching-20251103). Marco opened infra PR to add a temporary flag. CI triggered but a flaky test in infra pipeline caused a 4m delay.
- 09:30 — CI green. Canary rollout initiated (5%). Canary nodes reported degraded rejection rate improved to baseline. But traffic router did not apply canary->global promotion because label missing. Root cause: the rollout tool populates label key "canary_tag" but the router expects "canary_label" (mismatch introduced in infra#360).
- 09:36 — Manual promotion performed via Console by Sofia. Promotion proceeded, full rollout completed by 09:48. Post-rollout SLOs recovered.
- 09:55 — Initiated rollback exercise for separate simulated bad model push. Rollback API call worked; runtime stopped serving bad model. Noted KV-cache warmup: ~3 minutes of elevated p99. Need cache-warming strategy.

Decisions made during dry run:
- Add explicit validation step in playbook: verify "canary_label" observed in router metadata before relying on automatic promotion. (Assigned to Ethan, due 2025-11-10).
- Create a short-lived service-account fixture for dry-runs that auto-refreshes tokens. (Assigned to Jordan & Ethan, due 2025-11-07).
- Consolidate route/model primary dashboard: Observability team to create a single landing view named "Release Triager" linking Per-route metrics + ModelOps quicklinks. (Assigned to Marco, due 2025-11-12).
- Update CI pipeline: quarantine flaky infra tests (infra/test-loader) so hotfix CI path can proceed faster. (Assigned to Marco & Ethan, due 2025-11-08).

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Ethan Campbell: Update rollout tool to use canonical label key "canary_label" and add unit test to validate router integration. Due: 2025-11-10.
- Jordan Kim & Ethan Campbell: Provision dry-run service-account fixture with auto token refresh and document usage in playbook. Due: 2025-11-07.
- Marco Li: Implement "Release Triager" dashboard in Observability and add link in playbook. Due: 2025-11-12.
- Marco Li & CI team: Mark infra/test-loader flaky and create a fast-path for hotfix CI. Due: 2025-11-08.
- Priya Narayanan: Draft customer-facing incident snippet templates (hosted + dedicated) and place them in the playbook under "comms/templates". Due: 2025-11-09.
- Sofia Ramos: Run a second dry-run sim focusing on rollback + cache-warmup mitigation and measure p99 warmup time. Due: 2025-11-17.
- Aisha Patel: Update playbook doc with explicit checklist and attach Linear ticket RI-842. Due: 2025-11-06.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Cache-warming strategy: should we pre-warm caches on failover nodes, or rely on traffic shaping (ramping) to avoid p99 spikes? Need experiments. (SRE + Runtime)
- Authorization model for orchestrator: temporary tokens vs short-lived OIDC flow — which is acceptable for automated rollbacks? (Security + Platform)
- Should the canary label key be part of a shared schema (repo) with enforced linting? Proposal: add JSON Schema + test in infra PRs.

Notes on communications flow tested:
- Slack channel used: #release-hotfix (public) and #release-hotfix-escalation (private ops). We validated the escalation matrix (oncall -> engineering lead -> product PM -> CS lead). The matrix worked but there was confusion when product PM attempted to post the customer snippet; we need clear ownership in the playbook for who publishes external messaging.

Post-run metrics observed (rough):
- Time to pager: 3.5m (target < 2m)
- Time to patch branch creation: 7m (target < 5m)
- CI time to green: 9m (target < 5m); blocked by flaky tests
- Canary validation window: 6m (we used 5m target)
- Rollback end-to-end: 4m to stop bad variant but additional 3m p99 warmup

Suggested quick wins (can be done in next sprint):
- Add a pre-run checklist for oncall to confirm token freshness and dashboard links. Small doc change, low effort.
- Hard-fail CI on known flake causing delays only on hotfix path; or skip flaky test in hotfix context.
- Add a one-click "promote canary" button that validates label presence before invoking router promotion API.

Appendix: links to artifacts created during dry-run
- Dry-run trace: traces/2025-11-03/dryrun-release-01 (internal link)
- Hotfix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/372
- Linear ticket (tracking follow-ups): linear.app/RD/issue/RI-842

Notes to self / scribbles:
- consider adding a warmup probe that runs a short synthetic workload on nodes after rollback (10-30s) to pre-fill KV caches. Potential downside: cost and potential side-effects.
- Check whether Dedicated pools already have warm entrypoint for common models — ask Runtime team.

Next steps:
- Owners to update playbook and link PRs/tickets into this doc.
- Re-run full dry-run including token fixture and canary label fix w/ SRE observers. Target date for next dry-run: 2025-11-18.

End of notes.
